_note: Content bank for the Geometry Proofs practice section. Statement HTML may use XY for overlined segments and unicode ∠ ≅ ⊥ ° ½ ↔ →. Renderers must HTML-escape nothing inside statement (it is trusted author HTML).

reasons.name: Addition Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b, then a + c = b + c.
reasons.kid: You added the same thing to both sides of an equation.
reasons.trigger: added the same thing to both sides

reasons.name: Subtraction Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b, then a − c = b − c.
reasons.kid: You subtracted the same thing from both sides.
reasons.trigger: subtracted the same thing from both sides

reasons.name: Multiplication Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b, then a·c = b·c.
reasons.kid: You multiplied both sides by the same thing.
reasons.trigger: multiplied both sides by the same thing

reasons.name: Division Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b (and c ≠ 0), then a ÷ c = b ÷ c.
reasons.kid: You divided both sides by the same thing.
reasons.trigger: divided both sides by the same thing

reasons.name: Distributive Property
reasons.statement: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
reasons.kid: You multiplied across a sum inside parentheses.

reasons.name: Substitution Property
reasons.statement: If a = b, then b can replace a in any expression.
reasons.kid: You swapped something out for what it equals. Replacement — not a chain.
reasons.trigger: replaced something with what it equals

reasons.name: Reflexive Property of Equality
reasons.statement: a = a.
reasons.kid: Something equals itself. The most boring reason — and that's the point.
reasons.trigger: same thing on both sides of =

reasons.name: Symmetric Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b, then b = a.
reasons.kid: You flipped the equation around.

reasons.name: Transitive Property of Equality
reasons.statement: If a = b and b = c, then a = c.
reasons.kid: A chain: a equals b, b equals c, so a equals c. Chaining — not replacing.

reasons.name: Reflexive Property of Congruence
reasons.statement: A figure is congruent to itself: AB ≅ AB.
reasons.kid: Same idea as reflexive equality, but with ≅. Match the symbol!
reasons.trigger: same figure on both sides of ≅

reasons.name: Symmetric Property of Congruence
reasons.statement: If AB ≅ CD, then CD ≅ AB.
reasons.kid: You flipped a congruence around. Match the symbol!

reasons.name: Transitive Property of Congruence
reasons.statement: If AB ≅ CD and CD ≅ EF, then AB ≅ EF.
reasons.kid: A chain of ≅. Match the symbol!

reasons.name: Definition of Congruence
reasons.statement: Measures equal ↔ figures congruent: AB = CD ↔ AB ≅ CD; m∠A = m∠B ↔ ∠A ≅ ∠B.
reasons.kid: THE border-crosser: the ONLY reason that travels between = and ≅. If the statement crosses that border, it's this one.

reasons.name: Definition of Midpoint
reasons.statement: M is the midpoint of AB ↔ M splits it into two equal parts (AM = MB, with M between A and B).
reasons.kid: Midpoint named ↔ two equal halves. Works in both directions.

reasons.name: Definition of a Right Angle
reasons.statement: m∠A = 90° ↔ ∠A is a right angle.
reasons.kid: Translates between “90°” and “right angle” — nothing more.

reasons.name: Definition of Complementary Angles
reasons.statement: Two angles are complementary ↔ the sum of their measures is 90°.
reasons.kid: Translates between the word “complementary” and “adds to 90°”. It does NOT conclude congruence.

reasons.name: Definition of Supplementary Angles
reasons.statement: Two angles are supplementary ↔ the sum of their measures is 180°.
reasons.kid: Translates between the word “supplementary” and “adds to 180°”. It does NOT conclude congruence.

reasons.name: Definition of an Angle Bisector
reasons.statement: An angle bisector divides an angle into two equal parts.
reasons.kid: A bisector is NAMED → two equal angles. If no bisector is mentioned, this is NOT your reason.

reasons.name: Definition of Perpendicular
reasons.statement: Perpendicular lines form right angles.
reasons.kid: See ⊥ → right angles appear. That's the whole job of this definition.

reasons.name: Segment Addition Postulate
reasons.statement: If B is between A and C, then AB + BC = AC.
reasons.kid: A point BETWEEN two others → the parts add to the whole. Look for the word “between”.

reasons.name: Angle Addition Postulate
reasons.statement: m∠ABD + m∠DBC = m∠ABC — adjacent angles add to the big angle.
reasons.kid: Two small angles side by side → add them to get the big angle. Look for a ray splitting an angle.
reasons.trigger: adjacent parts add to the whole angle

reasons.name: Vertical Angles Theorem
reasons.statement: If two angles are vertical, then they are congruent.
reasons.kid: X marks the spot: crossing lines → the opposite angles are congruent. The definition only NAMES the picture; the THEOREM gives you the congruence.

reasons.name: Complement Theorem
reasons.statement: If two angles form a right angle, then they are complementary.
reasons.kid: The trigger is the phrase “form a right angle” — that phrase means THIS theorem, not the definition.

reasons.name: Linear Pair Theorem (Supplement Theorem)
reasons.statement: If two angles form a linear pair, then they are supplementary.
reasons.kid: The trigger is “form a linear pair” — side by side on a straight line → supplementary.

reasons.name: Congruent Complements Theorem
reasons.statement: If two angles are complementary to the same angle, then they are congruent. (If ∠A is complementary to ∠B and ∠C is complementary to ∠B, then ∠A ≅ ∠C.)
reasons.kid: Same angle in the middle, both complementary to it → the two are congruent.
reasons.trigger: complementary to the same angle → congruent

reasons.name: Congruent Supplements Theorem
reasons.statement: If two angles are supplementary to the same angle, then they are congruent. (If ∠A is supplementary to ∠B and ∠C is supplementary to ∠B, then ∠A ≅ ∠C.)
reasons.kid: Same angle in the middle, both supplementary to it → the two are congruent.
reasons.trigger: supplementary to the same angle → congruent

spotErrors.statement: If ∠X is supplementary to ∠Y and ∠X is supplementary to ∠Z, then ∠Y ≅ ∠Z.
spotErrors.why: The definition of supplementary is a two-way street: “supplementary” means “the measures add to 180°” — and that's ALL it does. It translates the word into math. It can never conclude that two angles are congruent. Here, two angles are each supplementary to the SAME angle (∠X), and we conclude they're congruent to each other — that exact if-then is the Congruent Supplements Theorem.
spotErrors.rule: Same angle in the middle → Congruent Supplements Theorem.

spotErrors.statement: Two lines cross, forming vertical angles ∠1 and ∠2. Then ∠1 ≅ ∠2.
spotErrors.why: The definition only tells you what vertical angles ARE — the opposite angles made by two crossing lines. Knowing the name of the picture doesn't prove anything. The Vertical Angles Theorem is the if-then you actually use: IF two angles are vertical, THEN they are congruent.
spotErrors.rule: Picture-word in the “if”, congruent in the “then” → theorem, not definition.

spotErrors.statement: If ∠M and ∠N form a right angle, then ∠M and ∠N are complementary.
spotErrors.why: The definition connects “complementary” with “adds to 90°”. But this statement's “if” never mentions adding to 90° — it says the angles FORM A RIGHT ANGLE. That trigger phrase belongs to the Complement Theorem, not the definition.
spotErrors.rule: “Form a right angle” in the if → Complement Theorem.

spotErrors.statement: If ∠L is complementary to ∠M and ∠N is complementary to ∠M, then ∠L ≅ ∠N.
spotErrors.why: Same trap as #2: the definition only translates “complementary” into “adds to 90°”. It can't conclude congruence. Two angles, both complementary to the SAME angle (∠M), concluding they're congruent — that's the Congruent Complements Theorem, word for word.
spotErrors.rule: Same angle in the middle → Congruent Complements Theorem.

spotErrors.why: Nobody said KM bisects anything — the problem never mentions a bisector or two equal parts. A ray splitting an angle is not automatically a bisector! Two small adjacent angles adding to the big angle is the Angle Addition Postulate.
spotErrors.rule: Adjacent parts add to the whole → Addition Postulate. No bisector named → not the bisector definition.

spotErrors.statement: If l ⊥ m, then ∠1 is a right angle.
spotErrors.why: The ⊥ symbol means perpendicular, not bisector — they both make “equal angles” energy, which is why they're easy to mix up. The Definition of Perpendicular says perpendicular lines form right angles. That's exactly this statement.

tellApart.title: The supplementary trio
tellApart.lede: Three reasons mention “supplementary”. Only one fits each statement — here's the tell.

cards.tell: The statement just RESTATES what “supplementary” means — translating the word into “adds to 180°” (or the reverse). No new conclusion.
The statement mentions a LINEAR PAIR — two angles side by side on a straight line — and concludes they're supplementary.
TWO angles are each supplementary to the SAME angle, and the conclusion is that they're CONGRUENT to each other.

tellApart.title: The complementary trio
tellApart.lede: Same game, one level down: three reasons mention “complementary”.

cards.tell: Just translating: “complementary” ↔ “adds to 90°”. No new conclusion.
The trigger phrase is “FORM A RIGHT ANGLE” — that's this theorem's signature, and it concludes the angles are complementary.
TWO angles, each complementary to the SAME angle, concluding they're CONGRUENT.

tellApart.title: = vs ≅: crossing the border
tellApart.lede: Some statements cross between = (measures) and ≅ (figures). There is exactly ONE reason allowed to do that.

cards.tell: If the statement crosses the = / ≅ border — in either direction — it's the Definition of Congruence. Always. (Worksheet #1 and #11 in segments, #12 in angles.)
Stays on the = side: a = a. If you see ≅ anywhere, this is NOT it.
Stays on the ≅ side: figure ≅ itself. If you see = anywhere, this is NOT it.

tellApart.title: Reflexive / Symmetric / Transitive: match the symbol
tellApart.lede: Three moves, two symbols. First match the symbol (= or ≅), then name the move.

cards.tell: Same thing twice with = : a = a. (With ≅ it'd be the congruence version.)
Flipped with = : a = b → b = a. (With ≅ it'd be the congruence version.)
Chained with = : a = b, b = c → a = c. Substitution REPLACES (RS = WX goes INTO an equation); transitive CHAINS.
